questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines& $\dfrac{x - 4}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 3}{3}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2}$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{x - 4}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 3}{3}$

$\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2}$

So,

$\overset{→}{a}1 = 4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\overset{→}{a}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1 = - 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 5 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{\left(- 2\right)2 + \left(1\right)2 + \left(1\right)2} = \sqrt{6}$

Shortest distance between the lines~

$= \left|\left(\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right)\left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right|\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(- 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{6}\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{6 + 5 + 7}{6}\right| = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6}units$

$= 3\sqrt{6}units$

Hence this is the correct option.

$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{- 3}$

$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 5}$

$a ≡ \left(4, - 1, 0\right), b ≡ \left(\lambda, -$1, 2\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} = \left($4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) - \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} +2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} = \left(4 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

So, the shortest distance is given by,

$D = \left|\left|\begin{cases}\lambda -4 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } - 5\end{cases}\right|\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } - 5\end{cases}\right|\right|$

$⇒ D = \left|\dfrac{( \lambda - 4 ) ( - 10 + 12 ) - 0 + 2 ( 4 - 4 )}{| 2\overset{^}{i} - 1\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k} |}\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{5} = \left|\dfrac{2 ( \lambda - 4 )}{5}\right|$

$⇒ 3 = | \lambda - 4 |$

$⇒ \lambda - 4 = \pm3$

$⇒ \lambda = 7, 1$

So, sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is $8$.

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines& $\overset{→}{r1} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \lambda \in \mathbb{R}, \alpha > 0$~and $\overset{→}{r2} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \mu \in R$ is $9,$ then~$\alpha$ is equal to_____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$\overset{→}{r1} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} -2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{→}{r2} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu \left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

If $\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{a} + \lambda\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{c} + \lambda\overset{→}{d}$, then shortest distance between two lines is

$L = \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d}\right)\left|\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d}\right|$

Here,

$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d} =8\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d} =4 \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{d}\right| =4 \cdot3$

And,

$\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{c} = \left( \left(\alpha +$4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, shortest distance is

$\dfrac{\left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot 4\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{4 \cdot 3} =9$

$⇒ $2\left(\alpha +$4\right) + 4 + 3 = 27$

$⇒ \left(\alpha +$4\right) = 10$

$⇒ $\alpha =$6$

questions.q: If the lines& $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{2 - y}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{α}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{β}$~intersect, then the magnitude of the minimum value of $8\alpha\beta$& is _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,

${L}_{1} = \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{α} = \lambda$

${L}_{2} = \dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 0}{β} = \mu$

For point of intersection

$2\lambda + 1 = 5\mu + 4 . . . \left(i\right)$

$3\lambda + 2 = 2\mu + 1 . . . \left(ii\right)$

$\alpha\lambda +3 = \beta\mu +0 . . . \left(iii\right)$

From~ \left($i\right)$~and~ \left($ii\right)$, we get~$\lambda = \mu = - 1$

Now, from~ \left($iii\right)$, we get~\alpha - \beta =$3$

Let~$y = $8\alpha\beta

$⇒ y = $8\alpha \left(\alpha -$3\right)$

$⇒ y = $8 \left({α}^{2} -$-3\alpha + \dfrac{9}{4}\right) -18$

$⇒ y = 8\left(\alpha - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 - 18$

So, Minimum value of~$y = - 18$~at~$\alpha = + \dfrac{3}{2}$

$

questions.q: Let $O$ be the origin, and $M$ and $N$ be the points on the lines $\dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 5}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x + 8}{12} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 11}{9}$ respectively such that $MN$ is the shortest distance between the given lines. Then $\overset{→}{OM} \cdot \overset{→}{ON}$ is equal to _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 5}{3} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( 4\lambda + 5, \lambda + 4, 3\lambda + 5 )$

And ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + 8}{12} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 11}{9} = \mu$

$⇒ N ( 12\mu - 8, 5\mu - 2, 9\mu - 11 )$

Now, finding $\overset{→}{MN} = ( 4\lambda - 12\mu + 13, \lambda - 5\mu + 6, 3\lambda - 9\mu + 16 ) . . \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now finding cross product of direction ratios of line we get,

$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}$& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 1 & 3 \\ 12 & 5 & 9\end{cases}\right| = - 6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k} \ldots . . . \left(2\right)$

Now, solving the equation \left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$ as they are parallel vectors, we get,

$∴ $\dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0} = \dfrac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8}

Taking \dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0}

$⇒ \lambda - 5\mu + 6 = 0 \ldots \left(3\right)$

Taking $\dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8}$

$\lambda - 3\mu + 4 = 0 \ldots \left($4\right)$

Solve \left(3\right)$ and \left($4\right)$ we get

$\lambda = - 1, \mu = 1$

So, $M ( 1, 3, 2 )$ and $N ( 4, 3, - 2 )$

Hence, $\overset{→}{OM} $\cdot \overset{→}{ON} =$4 + 9 - 4 = 9$

$
